name: cross_feeding_metacommunity
description: A reusable cross-feeding metacommunity module (Module L). N connected compartments, each a coarse-grained capability vector over a protometabolic function set, evolving under cross-feeding (byproduct of one feeds the next capability in a neighbour), horizontal transfer, and parasite/cooperator roles. Connected heterogeneous populations develop capability redundancy (robustness) and a collective repertoire single compartments do not; the emergent set's overlap with the anaerobic H2/CO2/FeS LUCA reconstruction is reported as a far-end boundary, not a target. Coarse-grained, deterministic reproduction (not wrapped ALife).

exchange_rate.description: Cross-feeding strength (use isolated flag, not 0, to disable)

parasite_load.description: Fraction of compartments that drain neighbours

isolated.description: Isolated counterfactual arm: no cross-feeding/HGT/parasitism (use this, not exchange_rate=0)

metacommunity.doc:
Deterministic cross-feeding metacommunity over N connected compartments.

Each compartment holds a coarse-grained capability vector over ``CAPABILITIES``.
``diversity`` sets how heterogeneous the intrinsic assignments are across
compartments (0 = every compartment identical; 1 = each a different random
subset). The process evolves the *expressed* capability matrix each tick under
cross-feeding, horizontal transfer and parasite drain on a ring network, and
emits metacommunity robustness (redundancy), the isolated counterfactual, their
difference, the mean per-compartment functional breadth, and the overlap with the
anaerobic LUCA reconstruction (a reported boundary). All outputs are overwrite
sensors; the capability matrix is integrated internally.

_contract.summary: Coarse-grained deterministic cross-feeding metacommunity: do connected, heterogeneous compartments develop capability redundancy (robustness) and a collective repertoire that single compartments do not — with the anaerobic LUCA reconstruction as a far-end boundary?
_contract.description: N compartments on a ring network, each carrying a capability vector over a small coarse-grained protometabolic set (conceptually the og-02 functions; NOT N heavy libRoadRunner networks). diversity sets inter-compartment heterogeneity. Per tick: cross-feeding (a compartment expressing a capability a neighbour lacks supplies the byproduct at exchange_rate/connectivity), horizontal transfer (a capability spreads to connected compartments at hgt_rate), parasite drain (a seeded parasite_load fraction drain their neighbours; the rest cooperate), and maintenance decay of acquired capability toward the intrinsic set. Emits the metacommunity robustness (functional redundancy), the no-exchange isolated counterfactual on the same seeded assignment, their difference, the mean per-compartment functional breadth, and the collective overlap with the Weiss-2016 anaerobic H2/CO2/FeS LUCA core reported as a boundary (not a target). Deterministic given seed; a coarse-grained reproduction, not a wrapped ALife engine.

outputs.metacommunity_robustness: functional redundancy of the connected metacommunity (dimensionless, 0-1)
outputs.isolated_robustness: redundancy of the same seeded assignment with no exchange/HGT/parasitism (dimensionless, 0-1)
outputs.robustness_gain: connected minus isolated robustness — the connected-vs-isolated signal (dimensionless)
outputs.luca_capability_overlap: fraction of the anaerobic LUCA core covered by the collective repertoire — a reported boundary (dimensionless, 0-1)
outputs.mean_capability: mean expressed capability level across all compartments and functions (dimensionless, 0-1)

math: cross_feed[i,k] = (exchange_rate/connectivity) * sum_{j~i} max(eff[j,k]-eff[i,k], 0)  (community sharing of a byproduct you lack)
hgt[i,k] = hgt_rate * max_{j~i}(eff[j,k] - eff[i,k], 0)  (capability copied from a donor)
drain[i,k] = drain_coeff * (#parasite neighbours of i) * eff[i,k]
acquired <- (1-decay)*acquired + cross_feed + hgt - drain ;  eff = clip(intrinsic+acquired,0,1)
robustness = mean_k 1[coverage_k >= R]   (coverage_k = #{i: eff[i,k] > thr}); a capability is robust only if >= R compartments hold it
assumptions: Coarse-grained deterministic metacommunity (reproducible given seed); honestly a reproduction, not a wrapped ALife/agent engine.
Each compartment is a capability VECTOR over a small protometabolic set, not an instantiated metabolic network — cross-feeding/transfer are explicit couplings.
Cross-feeding rate scales as exchange_rate/connectivity; acquired (non-intrinsic) capability decays toward the intrinsic set so it needs continuous supply.
The LUCA overlap is a far-end BOUNDARY (phylogenomic constraint on capabilities eventually acquired), never a fitting target.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
